_doc: JEANTET dating cabinet (#26, Wave C, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #32). One of Saint-Claude's oldest houses (family firm first mentioned 1775; 'since 1807' is the company's own export-stamp claim). Dates mostly by the company ladder + honest wide brackets — NO documented stamp cliffs or line intro years exist in our sources. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Jeantet.json (factory history, detailed) + pipephil logo-jeantet + jeantetusine doc (mirror). CONFLICT noted: joined Cuty-Fort 1988 (pipedia: 'merged in the Cuty Fort Group in 1988'; plant closed, city bought it 1989) vs 1992 (pipephil) -> both carried, bracket edges kept loose.

history_anchors._doc: 1775 Jeantet family firm first mentioned. 1807 turnery (wooden shanks for porcelain pipes + wild-cherry pipes) — the year the company's export stamp claims ('JEANTET Production since 1807'). 1816 firm named JEANTET-DAVID; 1837 corporation (collective name for workshops all over Saint-Claude). 1858 BRIAR pipe manufacturing begins. 1891+ integrated factory built, Rue de Bonneville 12-14. 1898 Maurice Jeantet restructures (+ Genoud workshop purchase). 1938 limited company + branch workshop at Montréal-la-Cluse (Ain, cheaper pipes). 1948: 107 employees St-Claude + 18 Ain. ~1950 factory modernized. 1969 PEAK: 30-35k dozens/year, 72 workers. Decline to 6-7k dozens, 22 workers by 1987. 1988 merged into Cuty-Fort (est. 1987, headed by Chacom; pipephil says 1992) along with Jean Lacroix + Emile Vuillard; CHACOM CLOSES THE JEANTET PLANT; the city buys the buildings 1989 (wrecked ~1992). Post-merger Jeantet = a CHAPUIS-COMOY-MADE SUB-BRAND. Yves Grenard was Jeantet's chief designer before taking over Chapuis-Comoy 1971 (artisan-registry link). 2000 Dominique Jeantet retires; 2010 the brand DROPS OUT of Cuty-Fort, label back to the Jeantet family, PIPE PRODUCTION DISCONTINUED.

brand_marks.physical: Early stamping: 'Jeantet' with a FLORID J. Arched 'Jeantet' later. 'JEANTET Production since 1807' (sometimes + CORSICAN BRIAR, Made in France) = EXPORT-intended pipes. Sir Duke line = Algerian briar, some meerschaum-lined. Octogonal + Olympic stem logos exist (undated). Maya line named after the 'Maya the Bee' cartoon.

line_years._notes: NO line intro years documented — identification-only lines: Sir Duke (Algerian briar), Duke of Kent, Grand Duke, Hermes, Sir Bruce, Antidote, Maya (named after the 'Maya the Bee' cartoon — its French TV fame is 1978+, a tempting floor but NOT documented for the pipe line -> unencoded lead), Luxe, Lumberman, Preference, Jumbos. The 1980 Jeantet catalog pictured on pipedia = future bracket source (catalogue hunter target).
